Resend's ease of use and comprehensive documentation allowed us to transfer more than 30 transactional email templates in just under three days

I had the chance to get hands-on with Resend during the private beta and found the dashboard DX features really helpful: HTTP logging, email filtering, and webhooks (with logging). Being able to create email templates in React is great, too.

We are using Resend for our new products at GuruHotel (YC19) and the experience is really impressive. It has never been so easy to create email templates. The dashboard is simple and clear, we love it.
I think if you're targeting developers, SES is your biggest competitor. Their very cheap pay as you go pricing is more attractive than Resend's monthly pricing.
Congrats on the launch but I can't see why I would go to this over Postmark. It's so easy to get up and running, templates are solid, they have Zapier integration and pricing starts free.

I have to say I'm impressed at the breadth of their SDK support (even Elixir) and how idiomatic they seem in each language... Pretty wild that Twilio Sendgrid doesn't even have a code snippet on their homepage.

Please for the love of god do not decide for me where I want to be. I signed up... and the UI kept auto-switching me back to the dashboard whenever I returned to the tab. There is absolutely ZERO reason for this functionality.

Deliverability is the #1 problem all developers actually face... low volume transactional email constantly gets spam blocked on major MSPs. In the end we tend to use SMS or Slack/Teams webhooks instead.
Besides the ability to write templates using react syntax, I don't see why developers would use yet another centralized service in production.
One of those hip and new things I mistrusted was Resend even though 'suddenly everyone uses it'. I'll wait a few years before even contemplating it.
They are a wrapper over AWS SES... Many companies are already solving the same problem, and then resend comes into the picture with the support of YC.
Database credentials in the dashboard..? How?

As an early user of resend, found it easier to use than all the other providers but now I have lost confidence in resend (our clients' emails being hacked is a deal breaker) and will be deactivating multiple paid resend accounts and moving to other big players.
From the very beginning, Resend's DX was superior and the messaging told me as a developer, 'We understand you.'

Now, you can integrate your Vercel projects directly within the Resend dashboard—automatically create a new API key linked to your domain and have it added as an environment variable in your Vercel project.
